name: code/explain-project
title: Explain a project
summary: Explain an unfamiliar project: entry point, folder layout, main modules and how to run and test it.
when: Use when the user wants to understand a project or codebase they did not write.
steps: Call list_files on the project root to see its top folders and what the project is made of.
Call read_files on README, pyproject.toml, package.json and Makefile; when one is missing, skip it and read the others.
Call glob_files with **/main.py and **/__main__.py to find the entry point; when neither exists, say so and read the top module instead.
Call file_outline on the entry point to see its functions and imports and which modules it loads.
Call file_outline on the two or three largest modules to see what each one is responsible for.
Call grep_files with def main and app.run to trace how the program starts and where the first real work happens.
Call run_command with the run or test command the README gives, such as pytest, and read what it prints.
Answer with the entry point, the folder layout, the main modules and the exact run and test commands.
next: The final answer must name the entry point, the folder layout, the main modules and the exact commands to run and test, marking anything that could not be read.
